items.title: Toward vulnerability-friendly destinations: A relational framework for inclusive destination governance
items.abstract: Tourism research has generally located vulnerability in particular travelers and treated inclusion as an extension of accessibility provision. This paper reframes vulnerability as a relational destination-level condition produced, intensified, or reduced through interactions between heterogeneous human capacities and destination-system demands. A structured integrative conceptual synthesis connects public health equity, human factors engineering, and tourism management. The resulting framework explains how unequal exposure creates person-system mismatch, how destination arrangements produce vulnerability through recurring interfaces, and how inclusive-governance capability operates both preventively by shaping system properties and responsively by coordinating intervention. Risk redistribution is specified as a distinct mechanism that follows risk reduction and the allocation of responsibility, workload, and cost, and concerns the pooling, transfer, or absorption of residual risk by actors with greater capacity. Five recurring exposure interfaces and four intervention dimensions are organized in an analytical matrix. The framework distinguishes proximal outcomes (participation, safety, dignity, trust, and wellbeing) from conditional destination outcomes such as legitimacy, loyalty, and competitiveness. The paper extends relational vulnerability logic to the destination-system level and provides a research agenda for inclusive destination governance.

items.title: Towards Explorative IRBL: Combining Semantic Retrieval with LLM-Driven Iterative Code Exploration
items.abstract: Information Retrieval-based Bug Localization (IRBL) aims to identify buggy source files for a given bug report. Traditional and deep learning-based IRBL techniques often suffer from vocabulary mismatch and dependence on project-specific metadata. In contrast, recent Large Language Model (LLM)-based approaches struggle to provide appropriate context to the model: they either restrict analysis to a fixed set of candidate files, overwhelm the model with repository-wide information, or rely on explicit bug report cues to guide context collection. To address these issues, we propose GenLoc, a technique that combines semantic retrieval with LLM-driven code-exploration functions to iteratively analyze the code base and identify buggy files. We evaluate GenLoc on three complementary benchmarks, including large-scale and recent Java datasets as well as the Python based SWE-bench Lite dataset. Results demonstrate that GenLoc substantially outperforms traditional IRBL, deep learning-based approaches and recent LLM-based methods, while also localizing bugs that other techniques fail to detect.

items.title: Towards Iterative End-to-End Software Development: A Feature-Driven Multi-agent Framework
items.abstract: Recent advances in large language model agents offer the promise of automating end-to-end software development from natural language requirements. However, existing approaches largely adopt linear, waterfall-style pipelines, which oversimplify the iterative nature of real-world development and struggle with complex, larger-scale projects. To address these limitations, we propose EvoDev, an iterative software development framework inspired by feature-driven development. EvoDev decomposes user requirements into a set of user-valued features and constructs a Feature Map, a directed acyclic graph that explicitly models dependencies between features. Each feature node in the feature map maintains multi-layer contexts, including business logic, software design, and code implementation, which are propagated along dependencies to provide context for subsequent development iterations. We evaluate EvoDev on challenging Android development tasks and show that it improves Function Completeness by 57.3% over the best-performing baseline, Claude Code, while achieving 16.0%–58.5% improvements over single-agent baselines with different base LLMs. These results highlight the importance of feature decomposition, dependency modeling, context propagation, and workflow-aware agent design for end-to-end software development. Moreover, our work summarizes practical insights for designing iterative, LLM-driven development frameworks and informs future training of base LLMs to better support iterative software development.

items.title: TracePilot: Self-Verifiable Framework for Decentralized Applications Fault Localization across Transactions
items.abstract: Decentralized Applications (DApps) serve as a critical technical underpinning for business logic and user interaction within the blockchain-powered Web3 ecosystem. However, DApps are prone to faults, and localizing these faults within their intricate and often interconnected logic is a particularly time-consuming process, frequently taking tens of hours and leading to substantial economic losses for developers. Existing state-of-the-art DApp fault localization methods, e.g., FaultSeeker, cannot capture cross-transaction fault logic and produce verifiable diagnostic reports. Therefore, security experts have to spend substantial time manually verifying results and devising fixes. In this paper, we present TracePilot, a large language model (LLM)-based framework that automates DApp fault localization in two phases: distilling global fault insights from transaction sequences and then performing focused trace exploration to isolate the faulty logic. Crucially, we propose a patch verification mechanism that treats attack-blocking patches as executable evidence for fault localization while flagging potential overfitting risks for expert review. This mechanism improves result trustworthiness and reduces manual verification costs. Evaluated on a dataset of 149 real-world cases, TracePilot achieves a 71.14% Top-1 Recall. In the single-transaction fair comparison, it achieves 72.73%, substantially outperforming the state-of-the-art method at 32.23%. On cross-transaction cases, TracePilot achieves a 64.29% Top-1 Recall. The proposed algorithm is being integrated into the contract security agent developed by Ant Digital Technologies. Moreover, to facilitate further research, our code and dataset are publicly available online: https://github.com/feiqiuaaaa/TracePilot.

items.title: Traditional and modern education systems in Ayurveda education: a critical integrative review
items.abstract: The evolution of Āyurveda education reflects a shift from an ancient, philosophically grounded educational model to a contemporary, institutionalized, competency-based one. Historically, Āyurveda was transmitted through the Gurukul system, a personalized, residential pedagogical model combining textual study with hands-on clinical training, emphasizing moral discipline ( Dharma ) and the Guru-Śiṣya Paramparā (teacher-disciple lineage). Learning was structured around the Trividha Jñānopāya (three-fold means of knowledge) and the cognitive sequence of Śravaṇa (listening), Manana (reflection), and Nididhyāsana (internalization). Colonial administrative frameworks and subsequent modernization transitioned Āyurveda education into a structured, time-bound, standardized university system. Today, under the governance of the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and guided by the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, Āyurveda education employs Competency-Based Medical Education (CBME), integrating digital technologies, Simulation-Based Learning (SBL), and objective assessment tools such as the Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE). This modernization has increased scalability, standardization, and interdisciplinary integration, but has also introduced challenges including faculty shortages, infrastructural constraints, and epistemological tension between traditional and biomedical frameworks. This integrative review critically examines the historical trajectory, pedagogical shifts, and comparative methodologies of traditional and modern Āyurveda education, giving balanced weight to the strengths and limitations of each system. It further examines the current landscape of technological integration, including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Virtual Reality (VR) in anatomical and clinical training, with attention to validation, cost, and governance barriers, and identifies systemic barriers to reform. Finally, the review proposes policy, curricular, and research-oriented recommendations toward a critically synthesized model of Āyurveda education.

items.title: Transformation of Social Studies Pedagogy through Artificial Intelligence –Driving Technologies and Students’ Motivation in Calabar Metropolis of Cross River State, Nigeria
items.abstract: This study examined the transformation of Social Studies pedagogy through artificial intelligence –driving technologies and students’ motivation in Calabar Metropolis of Cross River State, Nigeria. The research design adopted for the study was the pre-test post-test quasi- experimental design. The population of the study consisted of all the JSS2 students in the 15 public secondary schools in Calabar Metropolis. Through simple random sampling technique, 92 students were randomly selected from two secondary schools in the study area and they formed the sample size of the experiment (40 for the exp grp and 52 for the control group). Pre and post-test were administered in the two randomly selected schools which represent both the experimental and control groups. The instrument used for data collection was Social Studies Motivation Scale (SOSMS). The researcher prepared a note of lesson for the experimental group teachers while the control group teachers were allowed to teach conventionally with their notes. A twenty-item questionnaires were designed by the researcher to measure the motivation of students in the course of the experiment using Likert Scale. The instrument underwent face and content validity by two experts in the Department of Educational Foundation, University of Calabar. A justifiable reliability coefficient of 0.78 and 0.81 were established using Cronbach’ Alpha. Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) statistics was used to test the null hypotheses at 0.05 level of significance. All analyses were carried out using the SPSS application (Statistical package for social sciences). In order to arrive at statistical decision, the P-value (probability value) obtained from SPSS application was compared with the significance level of 0.05. The findings revealed that the mean motivation of students taught Social Studies with intelligence tutoring systems and automated grading systems instructional methods were significantly higher than that of students taught with conventional method. The study recommended among others that the state should organize training that will build Social Studies teachers’ skills in the use of artificial intelligence tools such as intelligence tutoring systems and automated grading systems

items.title: Transformative Pedagogies for Student Retention in Health Sciences Education
items.abstract: Student retention remains a challenge in nursing and health sciences education, where students must achieve academic, clinical and professional competence. Traditional content-driven pedagogies often fail to address diversity and engagement, contributing to disengagement and attrition among students. This chapter explores how student-centred, digitally enabled and collaborative pedagogies can improve retention in health sciences education. Drawing on global and African scholarship, it examines strategies such as collaborative learning, interprofessional education, simulation-based learning, reflective practice, and technology-enhanced environments to strengthen engagement and self-directed learning. It also considers the role of learning environments, learning analytics and artificial intelligence in supporting personalised learning and identifying at risk students. Using examples from the Global South, the chapter highlights how equity-oriented pedagogies, curriculum reform, faculty development, and institutional leadership can foster inclusive and sustainable learning environments.

items.title: Transforming STEAM Education in India Through Artificial Intelligence and Digital Technologies
items.abstract: The NEP 2020 is designed to promote an integrated approach to learning that will allow students to think critically, creatively and to learn across disciplines. Therefore, the inclusion of STEAM education (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) is emerging as one strategy to prepare learners for an economy based on digital technologies. The use of AI and other digital technologies such as digital platforms, virtual labs and data-based tools is enhancing and changing the way teachers and students interact within the classroom environment. However, there are several challenges in terms of equity, accessibility and the preparedness of teachers to integrate these new technologies into their curriculum and to develop the necessary infrastructure. This chapter explores how the use of AI and digital technologies is changing the delivery of STEAM education in India, including the current state of innovation, implementation challenges, and potential future directions consistent with the goals of NEP 2020.

items.title: TrapHunter: Exposing Covert Pathways in Trap Token Contracts
items.abstract: Standardized token contracts (e.g., ERC-20) form the foundation of digital assets. However, attackers increasingly abuse this standardization to disguise malicious trap tokens. Unlike obvious violations, these contracts employ a strategy of "deceptive adherence": they strictly adhere to standard protocols to evade detection while embedding covert logic to defraud users. To address this, we first systematize the trap landscape by proposing a novel taxonomy derived from the intrinsic functional lifecycle of tokens (Generation, Circulation, Persistence, and Observation). We then propose TrapHunter, a framework designed to identify these traps and expose covert pathways within these deceptive contracts via intent deviation analysis. Specifically, TrapHunter introduces a unified semantic representation combining Abstract Behavior Trees (ABTs) and Augmented Path Graphs (APGs) to normalize intra-procedural syntax and reveal hidden execution paths driven by inter-procedural state dependencies. Crucially, it bridges the semantic gap by leveraging LLMs to reason about the behavioral intent of deviations from reference implementations, followed by fork-based dynamic validation to confirm exploitability. Experimental evaluation on 269 real-world contracts with three LLMs (DeepSeek, GPT, and Gemini) demonstrates that TrapHunter effectively detects all six categories of traps, achieving an average precision of 81.8% and recall of 85.4%, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art tools.

items.title: Types and prevalence of digital harassment from external and unknown individuals and prospective associations with employee health outcomes
items.abstract: Abstract Digital harassment from individuals external to the workplace is an emerging occupational health concern, but evidence on its longer-term health consequences remains limited. This prospective cohort study investigated characteristics associated with exposure, its prevalence, types, employee reactions, and associations with health outcomes among employees in Danish workplaces. Data were collected through two survey rounds in 2024, completed by 991 employees. Digital harassment was defined as harassment, intimidation, verbal abuse, threats, or unwanted sexual attention delivered through digital media. Qualitative thematic analysis identified ten harassment types and thirteen employee reactions. Outcomes included burnout, psychological well-being, and self-rated health. Overall, 28% reported at least one incident within the past year. Prevalence was higher among public sector employees, permanent staff, and employees with longer seniority. The most common forms were condescending or offensive messages and false accusations, typically eliciting irritation, intimidation, shock, or emotional exhaustion. Adjusting for gender, age, and seniority, baseline harassment was associated with higher burnout symptoms (β = 3.28, 95% CI 0.54–6.02) and higher odds of low self-rated health at follow-up (OR = 1.69, 95% CI 1.05–2.72), but not psychological well-being. These associations were attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for the respective baseline health outcome.

items.title: Uncanny Valley in Conversation? Effects of Internal and External Human-Likeness on Intimacy and Trust
items.abstract: Conversational agents built on large language models increasingly converse like humans, expressing emotions and disclosing their own experiences. Human-likeness, however, has been studied largely as a matter of appearance—how human an agent looks. Language now also lets an agent display internal human-likeness by conveying an inner life, raising the question of how deeply an AI should express its own experiences—and whether that depends on its appearance. In a 2 (appearance: machine-like vs. human-like) × 3 (self-disclosure: none vs. low vs. high) between-subjects experiment, 193 university students completed a single, brief, fully scripted counseling session with an AI counselor prototype and evaluated it on six measures, controlling for prior mind perception. The effects of disclosure depth depended on appearance: with the machine-like counselor, intimacy and social presence peaked at low and declined at high disclosure, with trust and perceived authenticity showing the same direction—an uncanny valley-like pattern—whereas with the human-like counselor evaluations generally rose with depth. Deeper disclosure was not judged more inappropriate, and moderated mediation analyses showed that deepening disclosure from low to high reduced anthropomorphism—and, through it, intimacy and trust—only for the machine-like counselor. Internal and external human-likeness were read together: how deeply an AI should speak about itself cannot be decided apart from how it looks.

items.title: Understanding Automated Program Repair Agents through the Lens of Traceability: An Empirical Study
items.abstract: Automated Program Repair (APR) agents leverage large language models (LLMs) to autonomously diagnose and patch software bugs using planning, reasoning, and tools. Although these agents show strong performance on leaderboards such as SWE-bench, little is understood about how they take actions, where they fail, and how their behavior compares to human developers. In this paper, we present the first systematic analysis of these limitations using 5 state-of-the-art APR agents. We trace the full decision-making pipelines of the 5 APR agents across 500 real-world repair tasks, from issue description to patch validation. Our study reveals that, while agents excel at simple fixes, they struggle with logic-intensive bugs, often generating verbose, overfitted patches that pass existing test suites without solving the root cause. Test generation and regression test selection remain major bottlenecks, as agents fail to reproduce issues or run relevant regression tests. Moreover, many agents operate with primitive tooling (e.g. bash scripts) and do not have access to debuggers or program analysis tools. These findings highlight key limitations of current APR systems and motivate several directions for next-generation APR design, including but not limited to: (1) a shift-left approach emphasizing early, high-quality test generation and validation to reduce spurious fixes and improve semantic correctness; (2) richer, more integrated tool ecosystems; (3) diversified agent architectures that combine complementary strengths; and (4) benchmarks that prioritize semantic repair quality and test-generation fidelity over surface-level success metrics.

items.title: Understanding Learner Engagement and Persistence in AI-Assisted Interactive Climate Fiction Learning
items.abstract: Advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled educators to create increasingly sophisticated interactive learning materials, yet relatively little research has examined how learners engage with and persist in such interventions over time. This exploratory case study investigated learner engagement and persistence within a five-stage AI-assisted interactive climate fiction (cli-fi) intervention delivered through H5P activities embedded within the Moodle learning management system as part of an extracurricular sustainability initiative at an English-medium university in China. Participation, activity scores, completion data, and time-on-task measures were analysed descriptively across a five-week intervention. While learners who engaged with the intervention demonstrated high levels of engagement, reflected in strong activity scores and substantial interaction with the materials, participation declined markedly across successive stages, falling from 25 learners in Story 1 to six learners by Story 5. Descriptive improvements were observed in environmental knowledge scores among the small number of learners completing both pre- and post-tests, although these findings were inconclusive. The findings highlight a clear distinction between engagement and persistence, suggesting that engaging digital learning experiences do not necessarily translate into sustained participation. The study contributes to emerging research on AI-assisted learning design by emphasising the importance of considering persistence as a distinct outcome when designing and evaluating multi-stage digital learning environments.

items.title: Unpacking AI Agent Participation in Issue-Centered Collaboration in Open-Source Software Development
items.abstract: The increasing participation of AI agents in open-source software development raises questions about their role in collaborative processes. This paper investigates how AI agent participation relates to the structure and outcomes of issue-centered collaboration in open-source software projects. We adopt a process-level perspective by modeling issue handling as sequences of events and extending dynamic issue-pr entropy to distinguish between agent-related and non-agent-related contributions. Using large-scale issue event data from 83 GitHub repositories, we construct a project–month panel dataset and analyze associations between collaboration complexity and development outcomes. Our results show that agent-related collaboration complexity is more strongly associated with development output than human-only collaboration complexity, and is associated with fewer newly introduced defects. In contrast, its relationship with issue resolution efficiency is highly context-dependent. These findings highlight the importance of considering collaboration structure when evaluating the impact of AI agents in open-source software development.

items.title: Unsupervised Deep Learning methods for Analysing Acoustic Emission data
items.abstract: The foundation of track construction in Germany and many other countries is typically based on a gravel superstructure with railway sleepers made of prestressed concrete. Concrete has been approved as a material for sleeper construction for several decades. However, sleepers are exposed to weather conditions and changing temperatures, which can lead to erosion processes. Artificial intelligence methods have been successfully applied to locate cracking events in concrete structures. Typically, supervised learning is used to train deep neural networks on events identified by traditional triangulation methods. In this work, self-supervised methods are applied to raw acoustic emission data to evaluate information without prior labeling. We compare autoencoders that create rich latent space embeddings of the events with results achieved by using Self-Organizing Maps and traditional clustering on vectors created through feature engineering of the signals. This study analyzes data from over 19,000 events with 16 channels of sound recordings obtained in a static three-point bending test with railway sleepers. The high dimensional latent space can be visualized with dimension reduction techniques. This evaluation of the manifold of the embedded vectors indicates that location information is preserved by this embedding process.

items.title: Use of artificial intelligence (AI) in vegetable crops: A review
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging technology in vegetable production, enabling data-driven decision making and precision agriculture practices. AI refers to the intelligence exhibited by machines that can perceive their environment, process large datasets, and make decisions to optimize agricultural productivity. With the integration of technologies such as machine learning, sensors, drones, satellites, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and Global Positioning Systems (GPS), AI enables efficient monitoring and management of crop production systems In vegetable cultivation, AI technologies assist farmers in several critical operations including soil monitoring, climate assessment, pest and disease diagnosis, irrigation scheduling, and yield prediction. Sensors such as wind vane, cup count anemometer, rain gauge, lux meter, soil moisture sensor, and crop canopy sensors collect real-time environmental and crop data. These data was processed through data loggers and machine learning algorithms to provide accurate recommendations for crop management. Drone-based imaging systems and multispectral cameras further support precision farming by identifying weeds, nutrient deficiencies and disease symptoms at early stages. The use of AI in vegetables also highlights image-based predictive agriculture systems where captured images are processed through stages such as. image cleaning, feature extraction, and model training to detect pests and diseases. Several case studies demonstrate the use of AI in vegetable crops such as tomato, capsicum, and chilli for monitoring canopy growth, irrigation management. Additionally, robotic technologies in harvesting address labor shortages in agriculture. items.title: User Beware: Inaccuracy and Inconsistency of Large Language Models in Providing Precision Dosing Recommendations for Patients With Kidney Impairment—A Case Series
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence-based dosing guidance for medications in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (AKI) and receiving continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) is limited. Freely available large language models (LLMs) can generate confident, human-like outputs. The accuracy and reproducibility of LLMs in providing precision drug dosing recommendations in the setting of AKI and CKRT have not been evaluated. OBJECTIVES: We sought to characterize literature concordance and internal consistency of LLM-generated dosing recommendations for cefepime and meropenem in patients with AKI and receiving CKRT. METHODS: Six investigators queried the freely available versions of six LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, OpenEvidence, and Perplexity) from July to September 2025 using three standardized vignettes asking for dosing recommendations and rationale to meet prespecified pharmacodynamic targets: (i) adult with AKI not on dialysis receiving cefepime, (ii) child receiving CKRT and cefepime, and (iii) toddler receiving high-effluent CKRT and meropenem. To assess inter-iteration consistency, each investigator also prompted one LLM three times for each vignette. Responses were parsed for concordance with recommendations in primary literature. LLM "reasoning" was evaluated for use of pharmacokinetic (PK) equations, citation accuracy versus confabulation, acknowledgment of uncertainty, and recommendations for therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) for efficacy or safety. RESULTS: LLM-generated dosing recommendations varied widely. Mean concordance with literature-based recommendations was 63% (range: 28%-94%). LLMs produced variable responses to the same user upon multiple iterations, with variance in daily maintenance doses recommended ranging from 0 to 1000%. OpenEvidence universally cited relevant sources, whereas other LLMs leveraged sources inconsistently or confabulated them. Each recommended TDM, though only Claude consistently acknowledged its own uncertainty. CONCLUSION: Freely available LLMs produce highly variable and often discordant antibiotic dosing recommendations for patients with AKI and receiving CKRT. Although valuable for hypothesis generation and literature retrieval, LLM outputs should not be used in isolation for drug dosing in critically ill patients with kidney dysfunction.

items.title: Using artificial intelligence to mitigate global teacher shortage
items.abstract: Purpose This viewpoint addresses the systemic global teacher crisis – driven by burnout, unsustainable workloads and administrative attrition – and explores the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to reduce non-academic tasks. This piece argues that by using AI to help with administrative burdens, education systems can improve teacher retention, enhance individual student engagement and even support democracy. Design/methodology/approach This piece uses a conceptual and synthesis-based approach, combining a review of current literature with the author's firsthand narrative reflections as a veteran educator and teacher trainer. Findings The piece identifies the root causes of the teacher shortage: the overwhelming volume of non-instructional work. The analysis of the literature supports the use of AI tools to unburden teachers from non-instructional work gaining time to build robust relationships with students, increase the individualization of instruction, all of which can lead to better meeting the learning needs of their students. Finally, it allows for a better life–work balance that can mitigate teacher attrition and attract more quality candidates. Research limitations/implications This is a viewpoint article, and although it is supported by a robust review of relevant literature, it does not put forward new empirical evidence. Practical implications The practical implications of the piece focus on reforming the daily operations of educators' work by integrating AI to eliminate up to six hours of administrative workload per week, thereby reducing teacher burnout and mitigating the global shortage. Social implications The social implications center on safeguarding democratic foundations by stabilizing an endangered education system. Restoring work–life balance through AI helps attract and retain qualified teachers, preventing the systemic collapse of public schooling. Originality/value The originality of this piece is in its unique view of how to mitigate the teacher shortage by embracing AI tools rather than fear them. By using relevant national and international literature in conjunction with the authentic, lived perspective of a veteran educator, the piece provides a fresh approach to combatting the teacher shortage.

items.title: Validating LLM-Generated Expert Judgments in AHP Decision Support: A Preregistered Cross-Study Benchmark and Randomized-Order Audit
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are entering decision-support systems as inexpensive synthetic experts, yet their judgments are rarely validated against published human targets. We benchmark six LLMs on a source-audited corpus of 27 published Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) studies with a preregistered holdout of 22 studies, 21 reference-weight tasks, 28,783 valid benchmark calls, and study-clustered inference. Holdout rank replication was modest and model dependent. A diagnostic showed that fixed-source-order rank evaluation is confounded with criterion presentation order: reference vectors largely follow source listing order, and a model-free descending-order rule reaches a mean Spearman correlation of 0.735, outscoring every model. A prospective randomized-order experiment raised Claude Sonnet 5’s mean Spearman correlation by 0.46, and a registered follow-up with an exactly balanced schedule replicated that gain. For HCX-007, the model that tracks presentation order most strongly, the randomized-order decline was directional but not statistically significant (0.17, Holm p=0.16), and the follow-up was inconclusive about the average difference (+0.007, 95% CI [−0.23, 0.22]); its single draws continued to follow presentation order, and in an exploratory subgroup of six tasks with seven or more criteria its balanced-order accuracy was lower. Most holdout panels could be implemented only as repeated draws under a shared profile, and matched individual human data were limited to two tasks. Benchmarks for synthetic experts should therefore balance presentation order and evaluate aggregate reconstruction, individual human-likeness, and downstream ranking separately.

items.title: Value in app store metadata and user reviews: A dual perspective on quality of Parkinson’s and dementia apps
items.abstract: App stores provide a range of health applications for people living with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease (PD). Users like patients can access information from both manufacturer-provided app descriptions and metadata, as well as from user reviews. However, navigating this information to identify value-generating apps of high quality remains challenging. From a health technology assessment (HTA) standpoint, quality is defined by evidence-based medicine, safety, and user-centeredness. To explore the potential value of app store information available to patients, we conducted a descriptive, mixed-methods analysis of unstructured app metadata and user feedback from the Apple App Store and Google Play Store (as of May 2024). We analyzed 1,237 AD/PD-related apps which included 50 duplicates (resulting in 1,187 apps), utilizing descriptive statistics, content analysis, large language model-supported exploratory classification, and a topic modeling approach. In total, only about 2% of the apps claimed to be certified medical devices. Moreover, 24% of Apple apps and 14% of Google apps were in the “Medical” app store genre, among which we found that 63% of Apple and 54% of Google apps were patient-facing. items.title: Vector symbolic algebras for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus
items.abstract: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus for Artificial General Intelligence (ARC-AGI) is a generative, few-shot fluid intelligence benchmark. Although humans effortlessly solve ARC-AGI, it remains extremely difficult for even the most advanced artificial intelligence systems. Inspired by methods for modelling human intelligence spanning neuroscience to psychology, we propose a cognitively inspired ARC-AGI solver. Our solver integrates System 1 intuitions with System 2 reasoning in an efficient and interpretable process using neurosymbolic methods based on Vector Symbolic Algebras (VSAs). Our solver works by object-centric program synthesis, leveraging VSAs to represent abstract objects, guide solution search, and enable sample-efficient neural learning. Preliminary results indicate success, with our solver scoring 10.8% on ARC-AGI-1-Train and 3.0% on ARC-AGI-1-Eval. Additionally, our solver performs well on simpler benchmarks, scoring 94.5% on Sort-of-ARC and 83.1% on 1D-ARC—the latter outperforming GPT-4 at a tiny fraction of the computational cost. Importantly, our approach is unique; we believe we are the first to apply VSAs to ARC-AGI and have developed one of the most cognitively plausible ARC-AGI solvers yet. Our code is available at: https://github.com/ijoffe/ARC-VSA-2025 .

items.title: Virtual Mourning in the Metaverse: User Acceptance, Needs, and Limitations of AI-Based Memory Avatars
items.abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly shaping the ways in which people remember and grieve. While existing platforms and social networks primarily preserve static content, immersive environments such as the metaverse and advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) enable the creation of interactive, AI-based memory avatars, often also referred to as “griefbots” or “deadbots”. This study examines the perceptions, acceptance, opportunities, as well as psychosocial and ethical limitations of such avatars from the perspective of potential users. To provide an empirical foundation, an interactive prototype was developed and evaluated as part of a quantitative study (N = 33). These results were supplemented by qualitative guided interviews with experts in grief counseling, psychotherapy, and pastoral care. The findings paint a highly ambivalent picture: While respondents see potential in preserving life stories or in processing missed goodbyes, concerns regarding emotional dependence, difficulties in accepting loss, and ethical and data protection risks dominate. The Behavioral Intention to use the technology depends largely on Perceived Usefulness (r = 0.74) and Emotional Impact (r = 0.82), rather than purely on user interface elements. Experts emphasize that simulated interactions must not hinder the necessary process of letting go. The study concludes with recommendations for transparency requirements, time limits, and clear ethical safeguards for vulnerable groups.

items.title: Well-being and Buen Vivir: intercultural dialogue between etic and emic perspectives
items.abstract: This study aimed to analyze perceptions of well-being, happiness, and meaning in life among non-indigenous and indigenous participants from the Javaé and Karajá peoples, based on etic and emic perspectives. A qualitative, exploratory, and comparative design was adopted. Participants included 13 indigenous students enrolled in the intercultural education degree program at the Federal University of Goiás and 14 non-indigenous individuals living in the central-west region of Brazil. Data were collected through three open-ended questions addressing well-being, happiness, and meaning in life. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using initial and focused coding procedures grounded in constructivist grounded theory, supported by computational tools based on large language models. The findings revealed common categories across both groups, such as family and community relationships, meaningful work and teaching, physical and mental health, and realization of aspirations. However, these categories acquire distinct meanings across different cultural frameworks. Among indigenous participants, well-being was conceived as a relational, collective, and territorially grounded experience, integrating culture, spirituality, ancestry, and nature. In contrast, non-indigenous participants emphasized more individualized narratives, centered on personal progress, consumption, and immediate pleasures. These results highlight the importance of intercultural and decolonial approaches to psychological research on well-being and challenge the universalization of models derived predominantly from WEIRD populations.

items.title: Which Evaluation Strategies Help Students Spot Visual Misinformation on Social Media?
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background The rapid spread of visual misinformation online, intensified by advances in generative artificial intelligence, presents new challenges for adolescents' digital information literacy. Although students' difficulties in evaluating online information are well documented, little is known about how they assess different forms of visual misinformation on social media. Objectives This study examined the extent to which lower secondary school students can successfully identify different types of visual misinformation on social media, the evaluation strategies they use, and whether these strategies predict misinformation detection across types of visual misinformation. Methods The participants were 272 students in Grades 7–9 who evaluated social media posts containing visual misinformation, including manipulated videos, manipulated images, and AI‐generated images. Students rated each item's credibility and provided written justifications. Evaluation strategies were coded using a theoretically grounded scheme. Results Students were moderately successful in identifying manipulated images and videos, but struggled to detect AI‐generated images, which were often perceived as credible. Students relied primarily on evaluation of visual appearance and content, while source evaluation and corroboration strategies were infrequently used. Across all visual misinformation types, examination of visual features, knowledge‐based evaluation, sourcing, and corroboration strategies predicted misinformation detection. However, corroboration was the only strategy that reliably predicted identification of AI‐generated images. Conclusions Students mostly rely on first‐hand evaluation of visual appearance and content, but these strategies are inadequate for detecting realistic AI‐generated visual misinformation. Instruction should emphasize active verification strategies, particularly corroboration, and support students in coordinating multiple evaluation strategies when engaging with online visual information.

items.abstract: The Zircon Firefly is a breakthrough aerial VTOL platform, sovereign aerial vehicle, and advanced unmanned aircraft system (UAS / UAV) engineered to deploy next-generation firefighting drone and fire fighting drones technology at scale. Designed to operate as an autonomous small drone or coordinated autonomous large aircraft singularly or within a high-density swarm powered by AI swarm intelligence, the aircraft redefines global wildfire mitigation, bushfire suppression, bush fire fighting, fire prevention, fire management, and community safety. Being developed through rigorous digital twin modeling, CFD simulation, and aerodynamic evaluation of R&D prototyping, the platform replaces traditional, low-efficiency water bombing with continuous thrust-based suppression and Mechanical Flame Separation (MFS)—conceptually scaling the ground-proven leaf blower tactic into a high-performance aerospace defence force.Engineered to eliminate the critical "suppression gap" where traditional aircraft drop payloads and leave fire lines to refill, this high-powered platform utilizes massive, high-velocity airflow generated by commercial jet turbines and high-thrust Electric Ducted Fans (EDFs). This delivers persistent atmospheric inerting, combustion disruption, low-oxygen flame suppression, and high-velocity airflow suppression across any burning forest or grassland ecosystem. Operating as a waterless firefighting solution that delivers zero-chemical fire suppression, the Firefly executes high-capacity perimeter defence, Urban-Wildland Interface (WUI) shielding, and direct convective updraft penetration while maintaining complete thermal turbulence stability via a proprietary gyroscopic stabilization assembly.Built for versatility across all operational phases, the platform excels at rapid initial attack, high-intensity fire management, fuel load reduction, controlled prescribed burn containment, and indigenous cultural burn management. Real-time operational intelligence is driven by multi-spectral sensor fusion—integrating UV sensors for ultraviolet flame detection, LIDAR, Doppler radar, thermal imaging, multi-spectral optical sensors, satellite communications, 5G connectivity, and direct data links with deployed ground sensors. These systems will enable both piloted or fully autonomous systems including precise beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) operations for unmanned or uncrewed platforms, total real-time situational awareness through collision avoidance, provide extended flight endurance, and rapid five-minute in-field turnaround logistics.By suppressing major mega-fires before forest canopy destruction, the platform accelerates carbon reduction, curbing gigatons of wildfire CO2 carbon emissions, providing a massive carbon emission offset, protecting critical terrestrial carbon sinks, and preserving biodiversity, forest canopy preservation, ecosystem resilience, watershed protection, and catchment defence.As a patented sovereign technology and essential emergency services technology, the Firefly safeguards critical assets—offering non-stop critical infrastructure protection, utility corridor defence, power substation protection, and renewable energy asset protection. By mitigating catastrophic fire spread, the platform directly drives avoided loss economics, disaster loss reduction, disaster risk reduction, and climate adaptation. This delivers significant government expenditure reduction, insurance risk mitigation, insurance rate stabilization, and substantial economic cost reduction on a global scale.

items.title: WHY PYTHON PROGRAMMING IN PHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCE?
items.abstract: The rapid digital transformation of the pharmaceutical sector has created a growing demand for professionals who can combine pharmaceutical knowledge with computational and data-analytic skills. Python programming has emerged as a valuable educational and professional tool because of its simple syntax, open-source nature, extensive scientific libraries, and applicability in data analysis, visualization, automation, pharmacokinetics, pharmacovigilance, formulation research, clinical studies, bioinformatics, quality control, and artificial intelligence-assisted drug development. The revised B.Pharm curriculum introduced by the Pharmacy Council of India under the NEP 2020 framework recognizes this changing professional environment by including Basics of Python Programming for Pharmaceutical Sciences at the undergraduate level. This curricular development represents an important shift from conventional computer literacy toward structured programming, pharmaceutical data handling, scientific visualization, and computational problem-solving. The present review examines the rationale for incorporating Python programming into pharmaceutical education and correlates the revised curriculum with emerging requirements of the pharmaceutical industry. Particular emphasis is placed on the relevance of NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, data cleaning, CSV/Excel processing, pharmacokinetic datasets, adverse drug reaction analysis, dissolution-profile visualization, research data management, and introductory pathways toward machine learning and artificial intelligence. The review further discusses the potential contribution of Python competency to pharmaceutical research and development, quality assurance, manufacturing, regulatory science, clinical research, pharmacovigilance, and Pharma 4.0. Challenges related to faculty training, infrastructure, limited instructional hours, data integrity, validation, and responsible use of artificial intelligence are also considered. It is concluded that Python should not be regarded merely as an additional programming subject in the pharmacy curriculum, but as a foundational digital competency capable of improving data literacy, research capability, interdisciplinary collaboration, and industrial readiness among future pharmacy graduates. This article cover subject wisr role of python programming in pharmaceutical industries.

items.title: Wildlife Monitoring System Using GSM System
items.abstract: The increasing incidence of wild animal intrusion in agricultural areas poses significant risks to both human safety and crop productivity. This project, AI-IoT Smart Animal Surveillance for Human Safety, proposes a real-time monitoring system that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Internet of Things (IoT) to detect, alert, and assess the presence of wild animals near farms. The system utilises a Raspberry Pi equipped with a camera module and employs the YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm to accurately identify animals from live video feeds. Upon detection, the system captures the image, sends an email alert with timestamp and location to the farmer, and activates a buzzer to warn nearby individuals. Additionally, IoT-based health monitoring sensors such as temperature, heartbeat, and gas sensors are used to evaluate the physical condition and surrounding environment of the detected animals, aiding early detection of diseases or environmental threats. The system operates in real-time and ensures quick response to critical situations, thereby minimizing crop damage and reducing the risk of human-animal conflicts. It is designed to be cost-effective, energy-efficient, and easy to deploy in rural and remote areas. Furthermore, the system can be enhanced with features such as mobile application integration, cloud-based data storage, and GPS tracking for better monitoring and control. Overall, the proposed system provides a smart, automated, and reliable solution for wildlife surveillance and safety management.

items.title: Workplace health investment and employment adjustment public health evidence from CSR reports of Chinese A-share listed firms
items.abstract: This study examines whether workplace-health-related corporate practices disclosed in corporate social responsibility (CSR) reports are associated with firm-level employment adjustment. Using 12,669 firm-year observations of Chinese A-share non-financial listed firms from 2013 to 2024, we construct a sentence-level measure of CSR-disclosed workplace health practice intensity and relate it to employment growth and residual employment-adjustment volatility. The indicator captures the relative intensity of disclosed occupational health and safety, medical support, mental-health services, health promotion and working-condition improvements. In firm and year fixed-effects models, a one-standard-deviation increase in disclosure intensity is associated with approximately 2.4% points higher employment growth and 0.012 higher three-year adjustment volatility. The associations are accompanied by lower disclosed work-injury rates and employee turnover, and the volatility pattern is concentrated in positive residual adjustment and industry upturns. Instrumental-variable and sample-selection analyses yield estimates consistent with the baseline fixed-effects results and the proposed occupational-health service channel. The results support an interpretation of lower occupational-health-related labor frictions and stronger expansion-oriented employment responsiveness. The study contributes evidence on the labor-market implications of corporate resource allocation toward workplace health governance and provides a firm-level basis for further health-economic evaluation.

items.title: Zenodo Metadata — Be: Founding Business Proposal v2.0
items.abstract: Be is a proposed organization dedicated to making safe, professionally governed artificial intelligence emotional support freely accessible to people who need someone to talk to. Be proposes an AI emotional-support system designed around a foundational distinction: an AI must never confuse what it observes with what it infers. Version 2.0 further develops the proposal's framework for adaptive conversational communication through the principle Adaptive Tone, Fixed Boundaries. Be may adapt its tone, vocabulary, pacing, humor, warmth, and conversational style to meet an individual where they are, while maintaining fixed ethical and relational boundaries. The system should allow human-like communication without creating a false human identity, adapting the interface without fabricating the relationship. The proposal incorporates Red Tape Theory™ as a proposed safety methodology: Observe. Record. Question. Do not force the axiom. Interpretation must never be represented as observation. Be does not propose to diagnose users or replace licensed mental-health professionals. Instead, it proposes a professionally governed pathway through which an AI system may recognize when AI-only support may no longer be an appropriate level of support and facilitate access to human care. A proposed charitable human-care program, If You Get It, You Get It, would seek to use charitable resources to help people access licensed professional care when professionally established safety criteria indicate that additional human support may be appropriate. Version 2.0 expands the proposal's treatment of personalization as a safety boundary, including the distinction between adapting communication to an individual and constructing a misleading simulated relationship. It also addresses clinical governance, privacy, autonomy, human handoff, crisis safety, documentation, intellectual-property considerations, research and evaluation, and a potential future child-focused system provisionally called NewBee. This publication is a founding proposal and does not represent a deployed clinical service, licensed mental-health treatment program, clinical efficacy claim, professional endorsement, or completed charitable program. Be begins with the question: Where could this harm somebody?

items.abstract: Работната бележка продължава „Защо пирамидата на доходите в България е толкова стръмна“ и „Бързи институции, бавни структури“. Те стигат до извод в три стъпки: изоставането в производителността е вътре в отраслите и е най-голямо при местните фирми; при нововъведенията то е най-голямо в организацията на работата, а не в продуктите; вероятна причина е прекъснатият частен организационен капитал. Самото управление обаче не е измерено пряко. Бележката пита дали публичните институции могат да намалят времето и цената за придобиване на организационен капитал, без да заместват пазарния подбор. Предлага „институционална инфраструктура за организационен капитал“: доброволна диагностика, стандартни управленски инструменти, практическо консултиране, по-малка административна тежест за участниците и помощ при преструктуриране, продажба или прекратяване на фирмата. Показва, че процедурата по стабилизация в Търговския закон съществува от 2017 г., но между 2017 и 2022 г. е използвана само 12 пъти. Два полеви експеримента подкрепят управленското консултиране, но ефектите силно се различават между програмите. Затова бележката не предлага национална програма, а три пилота с предварително заявени критерии за оценка и прекратяване. Подготвена с помощта на ChatGPT (OpenAI) и Claude (Anthropic); числата са сверени с посочените източници. Пълен текст на български. This working note follows two earlier notes on Bulgaria's income distribution and on the historical layers of its economy. They reach a three-step conclusion: the productivity gap lies within sectors and is largest among domestically controlled firms; in innovation, the gap is widest in the organisation of work rather than in products; a likely cause is the interrupted stock of private organisational capital, although management itself has not been measured directly. The note asks whether public institutions can reduce the time and cost of acquiring organisational capital without replacing market selection. It proposes an "institutional infrastructure for organisational capital": voluntary firm diagnostics, standard management tools, practical consulting, lower administrative burden for participants, and help with restructuring, transfer or exit. It shows that Bulgaria's pre-insolvency stabilisation procedure has existed since 2017 but was used only 12 times between 2017 and 2022. Two field experiments support management consulting, but effects vary widely across programmes. The note therefore proposes three pilots with pre-registered evaluation and termination criteria rather than a national programme. Prepared with the assistance of ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Claude (Anthropic). Full text in Bulgarian.
